title: Add orbit collection flashlight script
objective: Implement a new flashlight orbit collection script from the approved plan: one new script with teleop target selection/orbit preview and render mode that reads a saved orbit spec plus JSON light settings and outputs one RGB MP4 and one depth visualization MP4 per light setting.
instructions: Ignore existing dirty .control-tower operational artifacts unless they block product work; do not edit .control-tower files.

Implement two modes: teleop and render. Teleop lets the user move normally, select a forward-ray target, run one visible viewport orbit on button press, then restore the original spectator pawn pose and controller rotation. Render reads a saved orbit spec and a JSON list of light settings and writes videos per setting.

Reuse existing flashlight controls from examples/flashlight/run.py: co-located spotlight, intensity/enabled state, yaw/pitch light offsets, D-pad aim keys, toggle key behavior, and IsInputKeyDown edge polling pattern.
Reuse camera capture and RGB/depth conversion patterns from examples/flashlight/run_programmatic_rerun.py and video writing patterns from examples/flashlight/render_flythrough.py.

Target selection: default select key Gamepad_FaceButton_Top; cast a forward visibility ray from the current camera pose. If a hit point cannot be obtained, fall back to a point on the camera forward vector at --fallback-target-distance centimeters and log that fallback clearly.

Orbit behavior: default orbit key Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom; orbit center is the selected target; radius defaults to current camera-target distance; one 360 degree orbit over --orbit-duration-seconds at --fps; camera looks at the target throughout; when teleop orbit completes, restore spectator pawn location and PlayerController control rotation to the original teleop pose.
Orbit spec JSON: teleop writes --orbit-spec-file and includes map/map_path, start camera pose, target point, orbit radius, duration, fps, image size, and light baseline settings.

Light batch JSON: render mode reads --light-settings-file as a list of objects with name, enabled, intensity, yaw_offset_degrees, and pitch_offset_degrees. For each setting write --output-dir/<name>/rgb.mp4, depth_meters_visualization.mp4, and frame folders.

CLI defaults: --mode teleop, --width 1280, --height 720, --fps 24, --intensity 30000, --attenuation-radius 1200, --inner-cone-angle 12, --outer-cone-angle 30, --light-yaw-offset-degrees 0, --light-pitch-offset-degrees 0, --movement-speed 1200. Preserve map/map-path mutual exclusion and positive numeric validations.
Keep v1 scoped: RGB plus depth visualization videos only; no Rerun stream in this new script.
Update examples/flashlight/README.md with concise usage for teleop target selection, orbit preview, orbit spec, light settings JSON, and render mode outputs.
If useful, add a small example light settings JSON under examples/flashlight/ with three settings; keep it reusable and documented.

Run non-simulator validation only: py_compile for the new script, JSON parse checks for any example JSON, and helper smoke tests for orbit pose generation/video path expansion if practical without launching SPEAR.
constraints: Do not modify existing product behavior in run.py, run_programmatic_rerun.py, or render_flythrough.py unless a tiny extraction or compatibility fix is absolutely necessary; prefer self-contained code in the new script.
expected_outputs: Builder ResultPacket summarizing implementation, changed files, validations run, and remaining live simulator validation steps.
definition_of_done: New script supports teleop target selection/orbit preview and render mode batch videos as specified.
README documents the new workflow and example commands.
Non-simulator validation passes or failures are clearly reported.
No git operations performed by Builder.
